data.body:
Split from B-rc-lifecycle (it grew past ~600 changed lines). Contract rows RC2 and RC9 (D-record-surface-contract).

(1) WEAKENING FLAG (RC2, D-decision-management 2): RecordKind already has an optional weakening(before, after) -> reason|"" hook (added by B-rc-lifecycle for merge). When the writer is an agent and the hook answers on edit/revise/remove/supersede/merge, the def.* event carries weakening=<reason>; the fold exposes unacked agent changes; `<kind> ack <id>` is an OPERATOR-ONLY verb (declared field operator_only on RecordKind, honoured by surfaces/exemptions.py: refused on MCP with an explained exit 3) writing ONE new event kind def.acked {kind, id, digest, by}, registered with its first writer and an upcaster stamp. B-dec-manage `decision ack` is an instance of this verb, not a second mechanism. `show` and `history` mark an unacknowledged agent weakening.
(2) READ-ONLY SOURCES (RC9): a readonly(record) -> reason|"" hook on RecordKind; every mutating verb refuses (exit 3) a record whose provenance source is an org bundle, naming source and revision and the local-override path. B-org-kinds registers the provider; with none registered nothing changes.
HOW TO TEST (failing first): an agent lowering a rule from block to warn is flagged until the operators ack, an operator edit is not flagged, ack over MCP is refused with exit 3 and the reason; a record from an org source refuses every mutating verb naming the source; old logs fold unchanged (golden); CLI and MCP bodies identical (test_mcp_parity); tools/list budget.
ACCEPTANCE: an agent-lowered enforcement shows as awaiting acknowledgement until the operator runs `rule ack`.
data.title: Record weakening flag, operator-only ack and read-only org sources on the record surface (RC2, RC9)

data.body:
SPLIT (fleet-trunk): items (7) weakening flag + ack and (8) read-only sources moved to B-rc-lifecycle-guard; this task keeps (1)-(6) and the RecordKind.weakening hook used by merge. Declined verbs now carry a reason (RecordKind.declined).

Contract rows RC1, RC2, RC3, RC9 (D-record-surface-contract). Operator 2026-10-11: "so the user or the agent can review, edit, delete, modify, split, evidence is logged".

WHAT: the record lifecycle, built once on the record surface, so goals, principles, rules, decisions, proposals and every later kind get it from their descriptor instead of writing it. Today api/records.py VERBS is list, show, add, edit, remove, search, revise. api/defs.py already has def_supersede and def_merge (and core/defs.py the def.superseded and def.merged events and the merged_from fold) but no surface offers them, `show` cuts the history to the newest 20 entries and keeps only digests (no before/after), a restore is only an unadvertised side effect of `revise`, and split exists for tasks only.
Add these to VERBS, generated on the CLI and as ACTIONS of the kind's one MCP tool (never a new tool; tools/list budget):
(1) `<kind> history <id> [--diff] [--limit N]`: the whole chain read from the log (not the fold's last 20): event, at, by, session, reason, digest; with --diff the field-level before and after (the def.* events carry `fields`; replay by lamport). Redacted, text fenced as data.
(2) `<kind> supersede <id> --by <id2> --reason` (wraps def_supersede; both stay, each names the other).
(3) `<kind> merge <id> [<id>...] --into <id2> --reason`: ONE log transaction: update the target (list fields tags, globs, links, categories are unioned; a scalar is kept unless --take <field>=<id> says otherwise; the text is the caller's: --text or the target's), then def.merged for each source; provenance both ways (the fold already keeps merged_from); refused when kinds differ, a source is not active, or the merge would drop a block-enforcement record into a weaker one without --allow-weaken.
(4) `<kind> split <id> --part <newid>:<field>=<value>[,..] (repeat) --reason` or `--from-file parts.toml`: ONE transaction: each part is a def.recorded with provenance.split_from = <id> (add-time duplicate check among the parts and against the rest, skipping the original), then def.retired of the original with reason and split_into = [ids]. Refuses a single part. No new event kind: split_into / split_from / restored_from are additive optional envelope fields the fold keeps in the history entry (D-compat: an older ddflow preserves what it does not read).
(5) `<kind> restore <id> [--to N|--to <lamport>] --reason`: re-records the fields of the chosen earlier version (default: the last active one) of a retired, superseded, merged or split record as def.recorded with provenance.restored_from; for a merged record the fold already drops it from the absorber's merged_from; for a split it restores the original and says the parts stay.
(6) EVIDENCE stamped on every def write (RC3): api/defs._envelope adds provenance.session (the agent's open session) and provenance.prompt (id of that session's latest session.prompt when there is one) beside `by`; additive. `show` prints them.
(7) WEAKENING FLAG (RC2, D-decision-management 2): RecordKind gains an optional `weakening(before, after) -> reason|""` hook (lower enforcement, widened override, status to retired/dropped/superseded, a guard removed). When the writer is an agent and the hook answers, the event carries weakening=<reason>; the fold exposes unacked agent changes; `<kind> ack <id>` is an OPERATOR-ONLY verb (declared field `operator_only` on RecordKind, honoured by surfaces/exemptions.py: refused on MCP with an explained exit 3) writing ONE new event kind def.acked {kind, id, digest, by}, registered with its first writer and an upcaster stamp. B-dec-manage's `decision ack` is an instance of this verb, not a second mechanism.
(8) READ-ONLY SOURCES (RC9): `readonly(record) -> reason|""` hook; every mutating verb refuses (exit 3) a record whose provenance source is an org bundle, naming source and revision and the local-override path. B-org-kinds registers the provider; with none registered nothing changes.
A kind may opt out of a verb in its descriptor WITH a reason (a proposal is never removed: reject and expire are its tombstones); the conformance test (B-rc-conformance) reads those reasons.

WHY (verified 2026-10-11): without this, five tasks each plan their own edit/retire/supersede/merge path (B199, B-rw-revision, B-coh-resolve, B-dec-manage, B-goal-model) and no task plans split or restore or a history view anywhere; evidence shown to the user is a digest, so 'who changed this rule and from what' cannot be answered after the fact; an agent can silently retire a block rule or drop a goal.

INTERFACE TO REUSE: api/records.py (RecordKind, _pre, _checked, _as), surfaces/records.py (the generator), api/defs.py (def_update, def_retire, def_supersede, def_merge, _envelope), core/defs.py and core/handlers/defs.py (DefRecord.history, merged_from), api/_dedupe.py, surfaces/exemptions.py, surfaces/history_verbs.py (render the new events), core/events.py (register def.acked with its first writer), core/upcasters.py.

HOW TO TEST (failing first): merge of two rules: target holds the unions, sources are status merged with successor, history on both sides names the other, one transaction (a failure injected after the first write leaves nothing half-done), replay is byte-identical; split into three: parts carry split_from, original retired with split_into, one part refused, duplicate part refused naming the other; restore returns the chosen version and history shows restored_from; history --diff shows before and after for three successive edits and is not cut at 20 entries; an agent lowering a rule from block to warn is flagged until the operator's ack, an operator edit is not flagged, ack over MCP is refused with exit 3 and the reason; a record from an org source refuses every mutating verb naming the source; old logs fold unchanged (golden); CLI and MCP bodies identical for every new verb (test_mcp_parity); tools/list budget test (raise TOOLS_LIST_BUDGET with a reason only if the added action text needs it).
SIZE: large (~800 lines + tests). Hot files api/records.py, surfaces/records.py, core/defs.py: B-goal-model, B-prop-model, B-rules-onto-record-surface, B-dec-manage, B-coh-resolve and B-rw-revision wait for this task.
ACCEPTANCE: on a throwaway repo, `rule add` -> `rule edit` -> `rule split` -> `rule merge` -> `rule remove` -> `rule restore` all work on CLI and MCP, `rule history <id> --diff` lists each step with who, when, why and session, and an agent-lowered enforcement shows as awaiting acknowledgement until the operator runs `rule ack`.
DOCS: docstring level here; the README section, the help topic `records` and the driver notes (when to merge, supersede or split) are written by B-rc-conformance (single editor of README and help.py).
